client_frame_short:
"Should we be worried that technology is still unsettled?" The news deserves attention, but **a pause is not a portfolio emergency**. This morning's futures are relatively steady, which is encouraging without proving that the uncertainty is over.

We can separate a company-specific leadership change from the health of a diversified portfolio. If your cash needs and risk tolerance have not changed, there is no need to trade simply because the headlines are uncomfortable. We are watching today's 8:30 inflation report and whether technology shares can hold their footing through the close.
client_frame:
The leadership change at NVIDIA is a real company-specific development: its November 12 announcement names Colette Kress interim chief executive while a successor search proceeds. The release does not establish an overnight publication time, so we treat it as prior-session context, not a new post-close shock. Applied Materials' timestamped after-close update, meanwhile, describes continuing AI-related semiconductor demand. These are different pieces of evidence, not reasons to assume the entire industry's outlook changed in one direction. (NVIDIA; Applied Materials investor relations)

At 05:51 ET, Nasdaq futures were essentially unchanged and S&P futures were up 0.18% against their respective prior-session references. Thursday's semiconductor index fell 0.54%, while the VIX closed at 18.70. Those are completed-session observations, not evidence of Friday capitulation or a current yen-funding squeeze. We have no verified dealer-flow or positioning data to support either claim. (Finance API; Polygon)

The policy backdrop remains restrictive. Against the verified 3.75-4.00% target band, CME's November 12 cohort puts December at 85.5% for a quarter-point increase and 14.5% for a half-point increase. The five-, ten- and thirty-year yield indexes are November 12 snapshots; the two-year CMT is a lagged November 10 observation. We do not combine those dates into a supposedly current curve. (Federal Reserve; CME; Finance API)

For clients: keep near-term spending reserves and agreed allocation ranges in view rather than responding to every headline. A calmer morning permits patience, not complacency. Today's 08:30 ET producer-price report is the next inflation checkpoint; renewed technology weakness alongside persistent inflation and financing pressure would merit a fresh risk review, not an automatic portfolio overhaul. (BLS calendar)
